Run controllers: informers, a work queue and a reconcile function

Source: R/manager.R
Manager.Rd

Run controllers: informers, a work queue and a reconcile function

Run controllers: informers, a work queue and a reconcile function

Details

A Manager runs one or more controllers in a single R process. Each controller watches a primary resource (and optionally the resources it creates), turns every change into a key on a WorkQueue, and calls your reconcile function with that key. This is the same model as controller-runtime in Go and kopf in Python, in one loop instead of threads.

reconcile(req) or reconcile(req, k) receives req, a list with key, namespace and name, and (if it takes a second argument) the Kube session. It should read the current state, make the cluster match what the object asks for, and return:

  • NULL (or anything else): done until the next change.

  • requeue(): try again soon, with per-key exponential backoff.

  • requeue_after()(seconds): look again after a delay (e.g. to poll something outside the cluster).

An error is logged with message() and retried with backoff; it does not stop the manager. Reconciles run one at a time, so keep them short.

Changes to owned resources (owns) reconcile their owner: the object named by an ownerReferences entry with controller: true whose kind and API group match the primary resource.

Public fields

kube

The Kube session controllers use.

Method new()

Create a manager.

Usage

Manager$new(k, poll_interval = 0.05)

Arguments

k

A Kube session (from kube()).

poll_interval

Seconds to sleep between passes when idle.

Method controller()

Add a controller.

Usage

Manager$controller(
  ref,
  reconcile,
  owns = character(),
  namespace = NULL,
  label_selector = NULL,
  resync_seconds = NULL,
  name = NULL,
  base_delay = 0.25,
  max_delay = 300
)

Arguments

ref

The primary resource, as for kube_get() (e.g. "pods", "example.com/v1:Site").

reconcile

function(req) or function(req, k); see Details.

owns

Resources this controller creates (refs). Changes to them reconcile their owner.

namespace

Watch only this namespace; NULL watches all namespaces (for namespaced resources).

label_selector

Optional label selector for the primary resource.

resync_seconds

If set, requeue every primary object this often, even without changes.

name

Controller name used in log messages (default: the kind).

base_delay, max_delay

Retry backoff bounds, seconds (see WorkQueue).

Returns

The controller, invisibly.

Method controllers()

The controllers added so far.

Usage

Manager$controllers()

Method start()

List every watched resource and open the watches. run() does this for you; call it yourself to drive step().

Usage

Manager$start()

Method serve_health()

Answer Kubernetes probes on port: GET /healthz returns 200 whenever the loop is turning, and GET /readyz returns 200 once the manager is running or standing by for the leader lease (503 before). Requests are answered between reconciles, so a reconcile that hangs makes the liveness probe fail. run() calls this for you when given health_port.

Usage

Manager$serve_health(port)

Arguments

port

TCP port to listen on (all interfaces).

Method step()

One pass of the loop: handle watch events, then run the reconciles that are ready. Waits up to max_wait seconds if there is nothing to do.

Usage

Manager$step(max_wait = 0)

Arguments

max_wait

Seconds to wait for work.

Returns

The number of reconciles run, invisibly.

Method run()

Run until stop_seconds pass or stop() is called.

Usage

Manager$run(
  stop_seconds = NULL,
  leader_election = NULL,
  lease_namespace = NULL,
  identity = NULL,
  health_port = NULL,
  ...
)

Arguments

stop_seconds

Optional time limit; NULL runs until stop().

leader_election

Name of a Lease to hold while running. When set, the manager waits until it holds the lease, reconciles only while it does, and stops if the lease is lost. Use this whenever more than one replica runs.

lease_namespace

Namespace of the Lease (default: the session's).

identity

This replica's identity (default: host name and PID).

health_port

If set, answer /healthz and /readyz on this port (see serve_health()), including while waiting for the lease.

...

Passed to run_as_leader() (lease timings).

Method stop()

Make run() return after the current reconcile.

Usage

Manager$stop()

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
k <- kube()
mgr <- Manager$new(k)
mgr$controller(
  "example.com/v1:Site",
  owns = "apps/v1:Deployment",
  reconcile = function(req, k) {
    site <- tryCatch(kube_get(k, "example.com/v1:Site", req$name,
                              namespace = req$namespace),
                     rk8s_api_error = function(e) NULL)
    if (is.null(site)) return(NULL)        # deleted; owned objects are GC'd
    # ... kube_apply() the Deployment it needs ...
    requeue_after(300)
  }
)
mgr$run(leader_election = "site-operator")
} # }
